info.name: Cyfuture DBaaS
info.description: DBaaS creates and manages the default organization in the backend. Project responses expose organizationId, and every project is server-bound to that organization. Immutable IDs (org-xxxx, prj-xxxx, db-xxxx) identify resources; database names are human-facing handles. Omit a database name to receive a unique engine-prefixed handle. Keep an Idempotency-Key unchanged only when retrying the exact same infrastructure request. The Backup and Restore folder supports scheduled full backups and PITR after KubeBlocks template validation plus a healthy observed recovery window.

item.name: Organization and Project

request.description: Returns the backend-managed default organization. If the seed has not yet run, the backend creates it with an immutable ID and a friendly display name.
Only displayName and description are accepted. The backend-managed organization ID, status, and project ownership cannot be changed by this API.
Only displayName and description are accepted. The backend assigns the default organization, projectId, and namespace internally. Omit displayName if you want a generated friendly name.

exec: pm.test('Project deletion returns a status', function () { pm.expect([200, 202]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Returns a status body immediately. DBaaS deletes project databases and removes the namespace after database cleanup is complete.

item.description: The organization is created and selected by the backend. There is no user-facing create, list, or organization-selection request. Users may only update its display name and description; projects are always bound to its immutable organizationId.

item.name: Database Provisioning

request.description: Deploys POSTGRESQL in STANDALONE mode. Run Database Options first to verify the versions installed on the target cluster.

Deploys POSTGRESQL in REPLICATION mode and requests automatic full backup during creation. DBaaS converts the backup schedule to UTC and later reports policy ACTIVE only after KubeBlocks generates an Available BackupPolicy and BackupSchedule.
Deploys MYSQL in STANDALONE mode. Run Database Options first to verify the versions installed on the target cluster.
Deploys MYSQL in REPLICATION mode. Run Database Options first to verify the versions installed on the target cluster.
Deploys MONGODB in STANDALONE mode. Run Database Options first to verify the versions installed on the target cluster.
Deploys MONGODB in REPLICA_SET mode. Run Database Options first to verify the versions installed on the target cluster.
Deploys MONGODB in SHARDING mode. Run Database Options first to verify the versions installed on the target cluster.

item.description: Create examples for all engine/mode combinations supported by the backend. Name is optional: omitted names receive a unique engine-prefixed handle. Each successful request stores databaseId and operationId for the lifecycle requests below.

item.name: Scaling & Expansion

request.description: KubeBlocks first prefers an in-place resize. If that is unsupported, DBaaS allows a replication-safe pod recreation. Poll Get Operation: it succeeds only after ready pods report the requested CPU and memory, and InstanceUpdateRestricted is surfaced instead of leaving the operation RUNNING indefinitely.

item.description: Project-scoped KubeBlocks OpsRequest examples. Set databaseId to a RUNNING database first. Vertical scaling uses PreferInPlace and safely falls back to a replication-aware pod recreation when required. For MongoDB sharding use componentName values such as mongos, config-server or shard.

request.description: Restarts every component in the database. Do not send a request body.

Disable deletion protection before calling this endpoint. DBaaS keeps the database in DELETING until the KubeBlocks Cluster and all database-specific credential/helper resources are gone; shared services and KubeBlocks child resources are not manually deleted.

item.name: Backup and Restore
item.description: Configure the KubeBlocks-generated backup policy before automatic backups or PITR. PITR requires a scheduled full backup and a READY recovery window backed by completed base backup plus healthy continuous coverage. Full and point-in-time restores always create a new database; they never overwrite the source. Keep each idempotency key only for a retry of the identical request.

request.description: Asynchronously patches Cluster.spec.backup including continuousMethod, pitrEnabled, and incrementalBackupEnabled=false. Cron is five-field and stored in UTC. PITR is accepted only for a supported installed full/continuous template pair.

Returns safe effective policy state, including observed PITR status and recoverable window. ACTIVE means the generated KubeBlocks policy and schedule are Available; repository credentials and Kubernetes identities are not returned.

exec: pm.test('Recovery window response is available', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

request.description: Returns observed PITR health and the actual recoverableFrom/recoverableUntil bounds. Only use POINT_IN_TIME restore when status is READY.

Requires a RUNNING PostgreSQL, MySQL, or MongoDB replica-set database. Returns the common AcceptedOperationResponse and stores resourceId as backupId. FULL is the only currently enabled type; retentionDays is 1-3650.
Lists safe backup metadata. Responses deliberately exclude object-storage credentials, encryption material, Kubernetes Secrets, and database passwords.
Lists the currently available/restorable Backup Set in a PageResponse. Optional filters include databaseId, engine, triggerMethod, backupType, from, to, and search.
Lists immutable completed, failed, expired, and deleted backup history without credentials or secret values.
Lists restore attempts, restore mode/time/base backup, and public endpoint readiness metadata without passwords, usernames, Secrets, or private endpoints.
Read-only safe BackupRepo summaries: name, provider, default flag, and readiness. Credentials, Secret references, and values are never returned.
Poll until status is COMPLETED or FAILED. DBaaS does not report COMPLETED until KubeBlocks reports the Backup resource successful.

Backward-compatible full-restore endpoint. It requires an available COMPLETED full backup, creates a new database through a Restore OpsRequest, and never overwrites the source. Use the database-scoped restore requests below for explicit FULL or POINT_IN_TIME mode.
Creates an asynchronous full restore into a new Cluster. backupId must refer to a completed full backup for this source database.
Run Get PITR Recovery Window first. restoreTime must be an observed, past UTC timestamp within a READY recovery window. The restore always targets a new Cluster.
Poll until status is SUCCEEDED or FAILED. A successful restore means the KubeBlocks restore, restored Cluster, managed credentials, and shared public route are all ready.
Use this new database ID for normal DBaaS lifecycle and connection requests after the restore operation succeeds.

Asynchronously deletes only the known DBaaS-owned Backup CR. Because its KubeBlocks deletionPolicy is Retain, object-storage data is preserved. It is blocked while a restore from this backup is active.
Explicitly changes only this known Backup CR to KubeBlocks Delete policy and removes it, allowing KubeBlocks to purge its backup content. Never use this while the backup is needed for restore.
